# Shawn Corvec: weather and climate diagnostics (scorvec.com)

> Shawn Corvec is a US-based meteorologist and atmospheric scientist working on numerical weather
> prediction, operational forecasting and the weather behind energy markets. This site holds his
> publications, two original studies, and live diagnostics built from open model and observation
> data, each with a methods page that states how the figure is made and how it is tested.

## About the author
- [About](https://scorvec.com/about.html): background and the data licences behind the site
- [Resume](https://scorvec.com/resume.html)
- [Publications](https://scorvec.com/research.html): peer-reviewed work on convection and physics
  parameterization, orographic drag and vertical coordinates in the Canadian GEM model (Monthly
  Weather Review, JAMES), and the tropical circulation of the mid-Pliocene (Climate of the Past)

## Original studies
- [Do AI weather models obey the conservation laws?](https://scorvec.com/aifs-aam-budget.html):
  budget tests of ECMWF's data-driven ensemble against its physics ensemble, for angular momentum,
  dry-air mass, water and energy
- [Why the atmosphere spins up in El Niño](https://scorvec.com/torque-enso.html): how angular
  momentum enters the atmosphere, mainly through a pressure difference across the Andes, from ERA5
  1959-2026 and 41 CMIP6 models

## Methods
- [Methods hub](https://scorvec.com/guides/): how every figure on the site is made, including the
  statistical tests and what is deliberately not shown
- Guides: El Niño monitor, circulation, stratosphere, sudden stratospheric warming outlook, MJO,
  tropical waves, atmospheric rivers, seasonal and subseasonal outlooks, model verification, world
  ensemble maps

## Explainers
- [Explainers hub](https://scorvec.com/topics/): E-P flux, mountain torque, atmospheric angular
  momentum, wave activity flux, eddy heat flux, sudden stratospheric warming, the Hadley cell, the
  dynamic tropopause
